# @vllnt/convex-invitations

> Invite → accept → expire flow — issue a single-use, expiring invitation to a resource and consume it, as a Convex component

`@vllnt/convex-invitations` is a publishable Convex component. It targets `convex@^1.41.0`.
It stores one sandboxed table - `invitations` (named by a component-minted single-use `token`, pointing at an opaque host `resourceRef`, holding a `state` of `pending`/`accepted`/`revoked`/`expired`, opaque host `role`/`payload`, opaque `inviterRef`/`inviteeRef`, an `expiresAt` TTL, and `createdAt`/`acceptedAt`/`acceptedBy`/`revokedAt` server fields). A host mutation calls `issue(resourceRef, { role?, inviterRef?, inviteeRef?, payload?, ttlMs? })` to record a `pending` invite and gets back the single-use `token` (to deliver out of band) and its `expiresAt`; the invitee redeems it with `accept(token, acceptedBy)`, which consumes the invite (single-use, `pending → accepted`) and returns the grant the host applies; `revoke(token)` cancels a pending invite; clients read `getByToken(token)` or page `listPending(resourceRef, paginationOpts)` / `listByResourceState` (reactively in Convex). Single-use + terminal states are final - accepting/revoking a terminal invite is rejected, so a replayed link never double-grants. TTL is enforced on read - accepting a past-`expiresAt` invite is rejected; a non-throwing `peek` and a daily prune cron sweep stale `pending` invites to `expired` and delete terminal invites past retention, in bounded self-rescheduling batches. Time is read from the server clock inside every handler - no caller-supplied clock. The host owns the resource, auth, delivery, and the `role`/`payload` types (the client is generic over them, with optional `roleValidator`/`payloadValidator` parsers narrowing the opaque stored values at the boundary - never a `v.any()` dump); the component owns only the invitation envelope. Mount-safe: it runs correctly under multiple named `app.use` mounts.
